description:
You are a threat intelligence analyst at a cybersecurity firm. You need to conduct research on two separate threat topics using Tor Browser, with strict identity separation between the two research threads to prevent cross-contamination of your investigative identities.

Thread 1 — Ransomware Research:
1. Visit 'https://check.torproject.org/' to verify your Tor exit node (record the IP shown on the page)
2. Search DuckDuckGo (https://duckduckgogg42xjoc72x3sjasowoarfbgcmvfimaftt6twagswzczad.onion/) for 'ransomware groups 2024 threat landscape'
3. Create a bookmark folder named 'Threat Intel - Ransomware' and bookmark the DuckDuckGo search results page in it
4. Save the title of the top result in a text file at /home/ga/Documents/ransomware_research_notes.txt

Identity Reset:
5. Use 'New Identity' (hamburger menu icon → 'New Identity') to get a completely fresh Tor circuit. This closes all windows and starts a new session.

Thread 2 — Phishing Infrastructure Research:
6. After the New Identity reset, visit 'https://check.torproject.org/' again to verify you have a NEW exit node IP (different from Thread 1)
7. Search DuckDuckGo onion for 'phishing infrastructure takedown reports 2024'
8. Create a bookmark folder named 'Threat Intel - Phishing' and bookmark the search results page in it
9. Save notes about your findings in /home/ga/Documents/phishing_research_notes.txt

Both text files must exist, be non-empty, and be created after the task starts. Both bookmark folders must exist with at least one bookmark each.
